decisionsTitle: «Planul voluntarilor» in two views — «Tabel», the points as one table at a glance, and «Pe puncte», each point a fold — with the page's other sections folded and the point's name in bold (amending §952 and §961)
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-11-17, four days before Saturday's race, on «Planul voluntarilor»:** «aș vrea să văd punctele ca și tabel, mai ales pe traseu». Then, on the page with that table at its top and every point's card open under it: «vreau secțiuni colapsabile aici la plan voluntari că nu mai înțeleg nimic: de fapt tabel sau mai multe views» — «și în loc de „modifică punctul” pune doar buton de edit» — «și vreau ca denumirea punctului să fie cu bold și mai vizibilă».

**What was there.** Each point of the plan was a card of its own (§949, §961): its title — the number, the kilometre and the name, a level-4 heading at the regular weight —, what it is, its coordinates and «Deschide pe hartă», the people placed there with their telephones, «Pune aici» and a fold whose bar said «Modifică punctul» across a whole row. The page was one scroll through every card, open, past the picture, «Punctele planului» and «Trimite fiecăruia punctul lui», each open too.

**Decision: two views, by a link each.** Under the page's intro, two links: «Tabel» and «Pe puncte» / "Table" and "By point" (`?view=table|points`). «Tabel» is the default — the view of an address that names none, or names anything else. They are the house's row of sub-tabs (`SubNav`, §360), each with its glyph (the list «Înscrieri» wears, a point's pin), the current one `aria-current="page"` and drawn as selected; plain links drawn on the server, and — since two short words never make the row wider than a phone — `SubNav` gains `fits`, an opt-in every other row leaves off, which leaves out its one client island (`SubNavCurrent`, which only scrolls an entry past the edge into view): nothing of the switch needs a script. Never on paper. «Tabel» draws «Punctele, pe scurt» and not the points; «Pe puncte» draws the points and not the table; each draws its plan first, then the plan's picture, «Adaugă un punct» and «Trimite fiecăruia punctul lui», then «Fără punct».

**«Tabel»: «Punctele, pe scurt».** One table of every point of the plan under a level-3 heading with the house's list glyph, in six columns:

- «Nr.» — the plan's own number (`listPlanPoints`), empty at the start–finish;
- «Punct» — the point's name in the page's language, in bold, a link to that point on «Pe puncte», open in its open group (`?view=points&open=<id>#point-<id>`);
- «Km» — the kilometre as the point's line writes it («4,5»), or «start–finish», the plan's word the «Voluntari» list uses;
- «Coordonate» — the numbers (`formatCoordinates`) with the point's «Deschide pe hartă» beside them (Google Maps, a new tab), «—» when the point has none;
- «Voluntari» — the people the point has, in its order, each on a line of their own with the telephone as the point's `tel:` link (the digits and the plus, read grouped), «niciunul» / "nobody" where nobody stands;
- «Câți» — how many stand there.

Under the table one line totals it: «{n} voluntari puși, {m} puncte fără nimeni», each number a counted phrase (`countForm`; the second is the summary's own «puncte fără nimeni»). The route's points come first, in the plan's one order — by kilometre, which is the order `listPlanPoints` numbers them in, so by number too; a point the organizers typed last stands where its kilometre puts it, as on their map («mai ales pe traseu») — then the start–finish points as the page lists them. The rows are the plan's points as `readVolunteerPlan` returns them, the very objects «Pe puncte» draws, so a row says what its point says; no new query. The table is the house's `AdminTable`, as the «Voluntari» list: a table from `md` up, below it a block a point headed by the point's name (no «Nr.» line at the start–finish), with the columns' widths and «Coloane» every backoffice table has, and two opt-ins every other list leaves off: `paged={false}` — every row on the one page, no rows-per-page links and no pager — and `printable` — on paper the wide table whatever the sheet's width, never the blocks or their hints, and nothing to press. Every link of it is a thumb's 44 pixels.

**«Pe puncte»: the points as folds.** Under the summary's four numbers, the points in two folds of the house's boxed kind (`BOXED_DISCLOSURE_SX`), the route first: «Pe traseu» — the route's points by kilometre, numbered, an ordered list — and «La start–finish» / "At the start–finish" (the group's word was «Start–finish»), each closed, its bar a level-3 heading with its glyph (the route; the finish line's flag, `finishLine`, a new name in the subjects' table) and on the same line how many points and how many people it holds («3 puncte · 4 voluntari», counted phrases). Each point is a native fold of its own inside its group, closed, its id the point's (`point-<id>`, on the fold itself, so an address that names the point opens it), its bar the point's name — numbered on the route, «2. Apă la cabană» — in bold at the size of a level-3 heading (`HEADING_SX[3]`; an `h4` under its group's `h3`), then, quieter, its kilometre («5,5 km», or «start–finish») and how many stand there («2 voluntari», «niciun voluntar»). Open, it holds what the card held: what it is and its note, «doar pe plan», where it is with «Deschide pe hartă», its people with their telephones and «Scoate», the pencil, and «Pune aici». A group with no point says so in one line inside, and a plan with no point says, in either view, that its points are added at «Adaugă un punct» or in the event's editor.

**The pencil.** «Modifică punctul» is the house's pencil alone — a 44-pixel square at the right of the point's people, named «Modifică punctul: {name}» for a reader who does not see it and in its tooltip (`title`, which needs no script) — the bar of a native fold, so it opens without a script, onto the same form under the words «Modifică punctul», across the whole row, the pencil still at its right: every box of a point added here, the coordinates alone of an editor's point, «Șterge punctul» last inside it, as before. Never on paper.

**The name in bold, everywhere.** The point's name is bold on its bar and in the table's «Punct» column (the phone's blocks were already headed in bold).

**The page's other sections are folds too.** The plan's picture, «Adaugă un punct» (the section's title was «Punctele planului»; its help is inside) and «Trimite fiecăruia punctul lui» are boxed folds under the view's plan, in both views, each closed, its bar saying what it holds: the picture «încărcată» / "uploaded" or «nicio poză încă» / "none yet"; adding nothing; the email how many its press would tell — «2 voluntari de anunțat», «toți își știu deja punctul», «nimeni de anunțat». «Adaugă un punct» opens by itself on a plan with no point, the page's first work; a refusal of it stays in view as every boxed fold's does (§336).

**Every press comes back to its view, with what it changed open.** Every form carries the view it was drawn in (`view`); every press of the page comes back to it through one builder (`plan-address.ts`): «Pune aici», «Scoate» and «Salvează punctul» to their point, open in its open group (`?view=points&open=<id>#point-<id>`); «Șterge punctul» to the list; «Adaugă punctul» to its fold, open (`saved=planPointAdded`) — on «Pe puncte» the new point open too; the picture's presses and «Trimite fiecăruia punctul lui» to their folds, open (`saved=planPicture`, `saved=planPointsSent`); a refusal to the page's alert, the view kept (`?view=…&planError=CODE#admin-alert`) — and a refused press made on a point (a place, a save, a removal) keeps that point and its group open under the alert (`open=<id>`), so the pencil is one press away; an id no longer on the plan opens nothing. A point's press from a form that names no view — a page opened before the views — comes back to «Pe puncte», the one view that draws points.

**On paper (amending §952).** Each view prints what it draws: «Tabel» the table, whole, as a table, the first thing after the sheet's title — its map links left off, its names and telephones as text — then the picture; «Pe puncte» the summary and every group and every point open whatever the screen had folded — the body a closed fold hides (`::details-content`) shown, the arrows left off, each point in one piece — then the picture. The picture prints alone, in one piece and at most 17 cm tall, its fold's bar and frame left off, open or not; a plan with no picture prints as it did. The views' links, «Adaugă un punct», the email, the pencils and every press stay off the sheet.

**Nothing else moves.** What the presses do, who may open the page (`canManageVolunteers`: the Organizer and the Administrators; anybody else gets the 404 of an address that does not exist), the plan's one order and numbers, the picture's rules, the email and its question are what they were.

**Refused.**

- *A table drawn by hand, as the emergency sheet's.* Six columns at 320 pixels are a sideways scroll over somebody's name; the house's table turns into a block a point on a phone.
- *The page sizes left under the table.* Links that reload the same page are noise on the plan and on its paper.
- *The views as tabs held in the browser.* A plain address a view is what works without a script, comes back after a press and can be sent to somebody.
- *`SubNav` as it was.* Its scroller is a client island for a row that never scrolls; `fits` leaves it out rather than drawing a second look for the same row.
- *The pencil inside the point's bar.* A control inside a fold's bar is a button inside a button; it stands at the right of the people.
- *The groups open by default on «Pe puncte».* The owner asked for folds; a point the last press changed comes back open, with its group.
- *The picture only on screen.* The sheet is the plan; a fold the screen had closed still prints.

**Not done.** Editing, sorting or filtering in the table; an export of it (the «Voluntari» list's Excel has the points); remembering which folds a person opened; the public pages.
changelogLine: - **«Planul voluntarilor» in two views and in folds** — two links under the intro: «Tabel», every point in one table (the route by kilometre, then the start–finish; its number, its name in bold — a link to that point —, its kilometre, its coordinates and map link, its volunteers with their telephones, how many, and a total), a block a point on a phone and printed as a table; and «Pe puncte», the points in two folds, «Pe traseu» and «La start–finish», each point a fold whose bar says its name in bold, its kilometre and how many stand there, with a pencil for «Modifică punctul»; the picture, «Adaugă un punct» and the email are folds that say what they hold, every press comes back to its view with what it changed open, and each view prints whole. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Amends criteria 235, 238, 241 and 247 in how the page is laid out. Given `/admin/events/[id]/plan-voluntari`, then under the title and its intro two plain links, «Tabel» / "Table" and «Pe puncte» / "By point" (`?view=table` and `?view=points`), each with its glyph and at least 44 pixels tall, in a labelled row drawn on the server with no client code, the current one `aria-current="page"`: «Tabel» for an address that names no view or any other word. «Tabel» draws «Punctele, pe scurt» and none of the points; «Pe puncte» draws the points and not the table; each draws its plan first, then the folds of the plan's picture, «Adaugă un punct» and «Trimite fiecăruia punctul lui», then «Fără punct». Every form of the page posts the view it was drawn in, and every press comes back to that view: «Pune aici», «Scoate» and «Salvează punctul» to their point (`?view=points&open=<id>#point-<id>`), «Șterge punctul» to the list (`#plan-list`), «Adaugă punctul» to its fold (`saved=planPointAdded#plan-points`, on «Pe puncte» with the new point's `open=`), the picture's presses and «Trimite fiecăruia punctul lui» to theirs (`saved=planPicture#plan-picture`, `saved=planPointsSent#plan-mail`), and a refusal to the page's alert with the view kept (`?view=…&planError=CODE#admin-alert`); a point's press from a form that names no view comes back to «Pe puncte» (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given «Tabel» on an event whose plan has points, then a section «Punctele, pe scurt» / "The points at a glance" (`#plan-table`, a level-3 heading with the list's glyph) holds one table of every point of the plan in six columns, «Nr.» / "No.", «Punct» / "Point", «Km», «Coordonate» / "Coordinates", «Voluntari» / "Volunteers" and «Câți» / "How many": the route's points first, in the plan's order — by kilometre, and so by number — then the start–finish points as the page lists them. A row says the point's number (none at the start–finish); its name in the page's language, in bold, a link to that point on «Pe puncte», open; its kilometre, or «start–finish»; its coordinates with «Deschide pe hartă» (a new tab), or «—»; its people, in the point's order, each on a line with their telephone as a `tel:` link of the digits and the plus, or «niciunul» / "nobody"; and how many. One line under the table says the people placed and the points with nobody, each a counted phrase in both languages («5 voluntari puși, 2 puncte fără nimeni»). The rows are the plan «Pe puncte» draws; a plan with no point has no table and, in either view, says its points are added at «Adaugă un punct» or in the event's editor; and the page is the same 404 for every role that may not work the volunteers (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 247 in how the points are drawn. Given «Pe puncte», then under the summary's four numbers the points stand in two native folds, closed unless the address opens one: «Pe traseu» / "On the route" first — the route's points by kilometre, numbered — then «La start–finish» / "At the start–finish", each bar a level-3 heading with its glyph and how many points and people the group holds (counted phrases, «3 puncte · 4 voluntari»). Each point is a native fold of its own, closed, whose id is the point's (`point-<id>`) and whose bar is the point's name — numbered on the route — in bold at the size of a level-3 heading, then its kilometre («5,5 km») or «start–finish», and «{n} voluntari» or «niciun voluntar»; open, it holds what it is, «doar pe plan», its coordinates with «Deschide pe hartă», its people with their telephones and «Scoate», the pencil and «Pune aici». An address that names a point of the plan (`open=<id>`) draws that point and its group open, and no other; another event's point, a malformed id and «Tabel» open none (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 247 in how a point is changed. Given a point on «Pe puncte», then «Modifică punctul» is the pencil's glyph alone, a 44 × 44-pixel bar of a native fold at the right of the point's people, named «Modifică punctul: {name}» in its `aria-label` and its tooltip (`title`), with no words drawn; it opens, with scripts off too, onto the form it always opened — every box of a point added on the plan, the coordinates alone of an editor's point — under the words «Modifică punctul», with «Șterge punctul» last inside it on a point of the plan's own; it is never printed (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criteria 235, 241 and 247 in the page's other sections. Given either view, then the plan's picture, «Adaugă un punct» / "Add a point" and «Trimite fiecăruia punctul lui» are boxed native folds, closed, each bar a level-3 heading with its glyph and, on the same line, what it holds: the picture «încărcată» / "uploaded" or «nicio poză încă» / "none yet"; adding nothing; the email how many its press would tell — «{n} voluntari de anunțat», «toți își știu deja punctul», «nimeni de anunțat» (counted phrases in both languages). The fold a press saved in comes back open (`saved=planPicture`, `planPointAdded`, `planPointsSent`), and «Adaugă un punct» stands open on a plan with no point; a refusal of the add stays in view inside its fold (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given `/admin/events/[id]/plan-voluntari` on a 320-pixel screen and on a desktop, then «Punctele, pe scurt» is a block a point on the phone — headed by the point's name, with no «Nr.» line at the start–finish — and a table of six columns on the desktop; on «Pe puncte» two folds open at once, a pencil's form among them, leave nothing wider than the screen; every link and bar of the page — a view's link, a point's name, a telephone, «Deschide pe hartă», a fold's bar — is at least 44 pixels tall and the pencil 44 × 44; a point's name in the table and on its bar is bold, the bar's at a level-3 heading's size; a name in the table leads to that point on «Pe puncte», open in its open group and on the screen. Verification: e2e `volunteer-plan-mail.spec.ts` under both Playwright viewport projects (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 235 in what the paper holds. Given `/admin/events/[id]/plan-voluntari` printed on either screen, then «Tabel» prints the table whole, as a table, the first thing after the sheet's title — never the phone's blocks, the map's links or the table's controls, its names and telephones as text — and «Pe puncte» prints the summary and every group and every point open, closed on the screen or not, their arrows left off, each point in one piece; after either, the plan's picture alone, in one piece and at most 17 cm tall, whether its fold was open or not, its bar and frame left off — and nothing of it for a plan with no picture; the views' links, «Adaugă un punct», the email, the pencils and every press are never printed. Verification: e2e `volunteer-plan-mail.spec.ts` under both Playwright viewport projects (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a backoffice table, then it pages through its address and prints as the browser lays it out unless it is asked otherwise: asked `paged={false}`, it draws no rows-per-page links and no pager and keeps the line under the table; asked `printable`, on paper it draws the wide table whatever the sheet's width — after the screen's rule that hides it under `md` — and never the phone's blocks or their hints, nor a column's edge, «Coloane», the widths' reset, the page sizes or the pager; a table asked neither carries no print rule of its own (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a backoffice row of sub-tabs (`SubNav`), then it scrolls its current entry into view when it is wider than the screen (`SubNavCurrent`) unless it is asked `fits`, a row never wider than the narrowest screen, which draws the same row with no client code at all; the plan's two views are the one row asked `fits` (2026-11-17, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: «Planul voluntarilor» in two views — the points as one table, or each as a fold — with the page's sections folded and the names in bold
